limitations: This is exploratory selection over four outer months; those months are already part of the ongoing v6 evaluation, so it is not a fresh untouched confirmation set.
Only the probability mixture is changed. Features, labels, training classifier, issue schedule and test rows are unchanged.
The ensemble rule shares weather inputs with the learned model; it is a useful physical benchmark, not independent evidence.
Overlapping issue windows remain correlated; the row counts are not independent samples.
The coarse 0.1 validation grid tests 11 weights per horizon. Validation weights may still overfit the preceding 60-day sample.

limitations: Exploratory outer test months July-October 2026 have been inspected in the broader v6 comparison; this is not a fresh final confirmation period.
The target comes from DFLD half-hour recorded OD, not certified movement logs; a one-hour publication lag is assumed.
Half-hour truth cannot reveal two transitions within the same half-hour bin.
The event direction is assumed to be the opposite of the OD known at issue; when half-hour truth at T disagrees with that known state, direction scoring can be wrong and those cases are retained.
First-event probabilities describe whether any change has happened by h. They are not marginal probabilities of OD25 and do not describe a second change after the first.
The cummax step is a fixed shape constraint; it can raise later probabilities and is not fitted on the test period.
The constant training prevalence is the Brier reference for the same cumulative event target; current v6 marginal OD probabilities are not treated as event probabilities.
Issue windows overlap in time, so event windows and row counts are correlated.
